summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 3,032 crore (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA rose 37.5% to Rs 222 crore, with a record Rs 524 crore of new business wins.
summary.overview: TVS SCS posted its first Rs 3,000-plus crore revenue quarter, with ISCS growing 17.5% YoY and GFS 34.8% YoY on India ocean freight volumes. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened 80 bps YoY to 7.3%, driven by the Europe turnaround in ISCS and India volume growth in GFS. Full-year revenue grew 10.1% to Rs 11,003 crore and adjusted PBT rose 166% to Rs 99.3 crore. Management guided ISCS margin to 9.5-10% and group margin to about 7.3-7.4% for FY27, with GFS rates the key swing factor. The CEO-designate's first call also marked the retirement of MD Ravi Viswanathan.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 2,283 crore (+17.5% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 8,238.9 crore (+9.6%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% in Q4, driven by Europe recovery and steady India growth; North America scaled up a large project live in H2 FY25.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 748.8 crore (+34.8% YoY) on India ocean freight volumes; FY26 revenue Rs 2,764.1 crore (+11.4%). Margin 2.4% in Q4 on volume growth and cost actions, but freight rates remain under pressure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected in double digits, possibly early-to-mid teens, with ISCS a strong contributor.
ISCS adjusted EBITDA margin expected at 9.5-10% in FY27, versus 9.3% in Q4 FY26.
Group adjusted EBITDA margin expected around 7.3-7.4% in FY27, dependent on GFS freight rate trajectory.
Medium term: ISCS margin of 10.5-11%; GFS margin to move toward about 5% within 4-8 quarters and settle at 6-6.5%.
Management expects PBT to grow sequentially every quarter; Swamy & Sons acquisition (completed in May 2026) expected to be margin accretive for India in FY27.
Depreciation and lease interest expected to change with a shift from long-term to short-term leases; ECL impairment expected slightly lower in FY27 than Rs 56 crore booked in FY26.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model; capital allocation prioritised to ISCS, with minimal fixed-asset investment beyond warehouses.
Lease portfolio shifting from long-term to medium and short-term rentals where operationally feasible; short-term rental charges and warehouse R&M rose in FY26.
Second site of a key North America project went live in Q4 FY26, raising Ind AS 116 depreciation to Rs 108 crore in Q4.
Swamy & Sons 3PL acquisition (FMCG and consumption supply chains in India) completed in May 2026.
Patent accepted for unified logistics platform; AI and robotics deployed in operations.
demand_pricing: Q4 new business wins were Rs 523.7 crore, an all-time quarterly high (21% of Q4 FY25 revenue); FY26 new business Rs 1,206.7 crore (12.1% of FY25 revenue).
Order pipeline Rs 6,100 crore; typical conversion around 22%, with a target of 23-25%.
Fortune 500 active customers rose to 100 from 91, with 9 added in FY26.
Average customer contract length: about 4-4.1 years in India, 5+ years in North America, about 7.5 years in Europe.
GFS: freight rates under pressure; management says volumes are more resilient than pricing, which is volatile due to West Asia disruptions. Company says none of its lanes are in West Asia.
North America growing at about 28.3% CAGR over five years, focused on industrial and auto accounts, with a goal of $50-60 million per large customer over 3-4 years.
Sectors with momentum include power (alternate energy), aerospace and defence (MOU with ALA), and China-plus-one relocations, which are still early.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ISCS growth, potentially 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports it if conversion rises from about 22% to 23-25%. It set expectations at double-digit, early-to-mid-teens growth, and aspires to get closer to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: ISCS 9.5-10% from 9.3% in Q4; group about 7.3-7.4%, with GFS freight rates the main variable and management cautious on GFS.

qa_highlights.question: Why was part of the labour-code provision taken in Q4 rather than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: A Labour Ministry clarification on 16 March came after Q3 results, requiring a reassessment and a Rs 5.2 crore additional provision in Q4. The company says the clarifications are now fully provided for.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impairment loss on financial instruments of about Rs 17.6 crore, and what is the FY27 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an expected credit loss provision on customers, Rs 56 crore booked in FY26. Management expects the rate to be slightly lower in FY27, as most customers are highly rated B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China-plus-one opportunity material?
qa_highlights.answer: Early traction with existing customers, including an earthmoving equipment company, but deals are not yet deep. Management is waiting to see whether US buyers accelerate expansion in India.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term targets for GFS and group revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not endorse a Rs 15,000 crore target by FY29-30; its long-term aspiration is early-teens EBITDA margins, with the GFS margin reaching 6-6.5%, the leader deferring to the incoming CEO.

risks_watch: GFS freight rate volatility from West Asia disruptions; management says volumes are resilient but pricing is volatile.
Ability to lift the pipeline conversion rate from about 22% to 23-25%.
Sustaining the Europe recovery and the North America project ramp.
Labour code provisions still have grey areas and interpretation risk.
Leadership transition: MD Ravi Viswanathan retiring; Vikas Chadha (Global CEO and MD designate) takes over.
Lease cost trend and rising short-term rental and R&M costs in warehousing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on ISCS growth, new wins and margin expansion, with the closing remarks calling the year a spectacular finish. Cautious and noncommittal on GFS pricing and freight rates, with management declining to speculate on Q1 FY27 or long-term revenue targets.
key_quotes: I'm pleased to share that we have delivered on our commitment that we made in the previous quarter on our quarter 4 growth, particularly in the ISCS segment.
It is important to call out that the GFS business continues to operate at structurally lower margins and the global freight industry is currently facing a period of uncertainty.
We have to get the PBT number growing every quarter and very confident that we will do that.
Our typical conversion like we have said in the past, has been around 22%.
